headline: Google has launched Playground, an experimental tool that lets people build and share browser games by describing them in everyday language.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: official launch of a consumer vibe-coding tool, but experimental and limited to US adults with a paid plan.
importance_line: People with no programming skills can make and share simple games, but for now only US adults with a Google AI subscription can use it, and the Unity integration is not yet available.
summary: Thurrott.com reports that Google software engineer Maryam Karimzadehgan announced Playground, a tool in which users create games by typing what they want, remix other people's games and share them, with leaderboards and multiplayer in some genres. It requires a Google AI subscription and is limited to US users aged 18 and over, and a Unity Spark integration is planned in a closed beta.
notes: Google's own post was not opened; Thurrott quotes the announcement.
